pattern.name: checking_pr_status
pattern.usage: A set of commands to quickly assess the state of a Pull Request.

pattern.name: analyzing_failing_tests
pattern.usage: Commands to investigate why a specific test is failing.

template.comment: Check PR mergeable status
If mergeable is false or mergeStateStatus is CONFLICTING, delegate to code with nayan-conflict-resolution skill

pattern.name: delegating_conflict_resolution
pattern.usage: Delegate merge conflict resolution to code mode with nayan-conflict-resolution skill.

template.comment: When conflicts are detected, create a new task for code with nayan-conflict-resolution skill
template.command: <new_task> <mode>code</mode> <message>Resolve merge conflicts for PR #<pr_number>. Use nayan-conflict-resolution skill methodology.</message> </new_task>
template.comment: Wait for code to complete conflict resolution before continuing with other fixes

pattern.name: checking_out_pr
pattern.usage: Check out a pull request branch locally.

template.comment: Alternative if gh checkout fails:
template.command: git fetch origin pull/<pr_number>/head:<branch_name> && git checkout <branch_name>

pattern.name: determine_push_remote
pattern.usage: Determine the correct remote to push to (handles forks).

template.comment: Get PR metadata to check if it's from a fork
If isCrossRepository is true, it's from a fork
Check if fork remote exists, otherwise add it
Use appropriate remote based on PR source

pattern.name: real_time_monitoring
pattern.usage: Monitor PR checks in real-time as they run.

template.comment: Continuously monitor check status with automatic updates
template.alternative: For one-time status check: gh pr checks <pr_number> --json state,conclusion,name,detailsUrl

pattern.name: safe_push_operations
pattern.usage: Push operations that handle both origin and fork remotes correctly.

template.comment: First determine the correct remote (origin or fork)
If isCrossRepository is false, push to origin
If isCrossRepository is true, push to fork remote
If force-with-lease fails, fetch and retry

pattern.name: automated_commit_operations
pattern.usage: Commit operations that work in automated environments while respecting .gitignore.

template.comment: Review what files have been modified
Add only tracked files that were modified (respects .gitignore)
If you need to add specific new files, list them explicitly

pattern.name: safe_file_staging
pattern.usage: Safely stage files for commit while avoiding temporary files and respecting .gitignore.

template.comment: First, check what files are currently modified or untracked
Review the output to identify files that should NOT be committed:
- Files starting with . (hidden files like .DS_Store, .swp)
- Build artifacts (dist/, build/, *.pyc, *.o)
- IDE files (.idea/, .vscode/, *.iml)
- Temporary files (*.tmp, *.temp, *~)
Option 1: Stage only modified tracked files (safest)
Option 2: Stage specific files by path
Option 3: Use pathspec to add files matching a pattern
Option 4: Interactive staging to review each change
Always verify what's staged before committing
